name: Saints Peter and Paul
history: The fisherman Christ made the rock of His Church, and the persecutor He made the apostle to the nations. Both were martyred in Rome under Nero, Peter crucified, by tradition upside down, near the Vatican Hill, and Paul beheaded on the road to Ostia. The Church has kept their feast together on this day since at least the third century.
life: Simon of Bethsaida left his nets at Christ’s word, confessed Him as the Son of the living God, and received the name Peter and the keys of the kingdom. He denied his Lord three times and three times was asked, ‘Do you love me?’ After Pentecost he led the Church in Jerusalem and, by ancient tradition, came at last to Rome. Saul of Tarsus, a zealous Pharisee, was thrown to the ground on the road to Damascus and rose an apostle. He crossed the Mediterranean founding churches and wrote the letters that form much of the New Testament. Writing near the end, he said, ‘I have fought the good fight, I have finished the course, I have kept the faith.’ Excavations beneath Saint Peter’s in the twentieth century uncovered the ancient shrine over Peter’s grave, and Paul lies beneath the basilica that bears his name outside the walls.
prayerTo: Saint Peter and Saint Paul, pillars of the Church, one who fell and was forgiven, one who persecuted and was called, pray for the Pope and for the whole Church. Give me Peter’s love and Paul’s zeal, and help me to keep the faith to the end. Amen.
penance: Go to Mass for this solemnity and pray for the Pope by name. Make an act of contrition for the times you have denied Christ, as Peter did.
meditation: Christ asked Peter only one question after the Resurrection: do you love me? Hear Him ask you the same.
prayer: O God, Who made this day holy by the martyrdom of Your Apostles Peter and Paul, grant Your Church to follow in all things the teaching of those from whom she first received the faith. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
